mappings.note: Ramanuja's break from Shankara: world and souls real, bhakti as the path. A new religious-philosophical position, LO-58; LO-59 is rejected because no devotional verse is being read.
Chahamana resistance, with Prithviraja III checking Ghuri at the First Battle of Tarain in 1191. Military strategy and its limits, LO-55.
Kakatiya culture: Telugu and Sanskrit patronage alongside the Warangal fort's stone gateways and the Thousand Pillar temple. LO-57 for the architecture, LO-55 for the dynasty's patronage.
Whether the period shows resilience - trade continuing and temple building expanding despite northern invasions. A judgement about the period as a whole, goal-level CG-SST2.
Angkor Wat as evidence of exchange. LO-57 for Indian temple form carried abroad, CG-SST2 for the cultural transmission it attests.
The anubhava mandapa as an open pavilion for all backgrounds. LO-58 for the reform movement that built it, LO-60 for the equality that is its whole point.

The Ghaznavid invasions' effect on intellectual life, with al-Biruni recording scholars fleeing to Kashmir and Varanasi. CG-SST2 for the intellectual consequence and the source, LO-55 for the campaigns themselves.
The Khyber Pass as trade corridor and defensive chokepoint held by the Hindu Shahis. LO-55 for its use in defence, CG-SST1 for the terrain that makes it decisive.
Al-Biruni's survey of Indian religion, philosophy, geography and mathematics, and his Yogasutras translation. Sources and the transmission of knowledge, goal-level CG-SST2.
Hoysala architecture at Belur and Halebidu plus their literary patronage. LO-57 for the temples, LO-55 for the dynasty's cultural policy.
Rajendra I projecting power abroad - Sri Lanka, the Srivijaya expedition, merchant-guild backing, trade routes secured. Military strategy in the service of commerce, LO-55.
Bhoja's many-sided record: expansion, the Bhopal lake, treatises, and Dhara as a centre of learning. LO-55 for rule and public works, LO-57 for the architectural treatises he is remembered by.

Contrasts Mahmud's raid-and-withdraw with Ghuri's conquest. A direct LO-56 fit - comparison between two rulers' policies. (The stored answer breaks off and runs into a Basaveshvara fragment; see report.)

Case study resolving to Bakhtiyar Khilji destroying Nalanda in the belief it was a fortress. LO-55 for the campaign, C-SST2.3 at competency level for part (c) on Buddhism's decline, which LO-58 cannot take since it covers emergence.

Case study on a scholar who learned the local language and translated its philosophy while the army he travelled with destroyed - al-Biruni and Sanskrit. Source, method and contrast, goal-level CG-SST2.
Case study on a punitive naval expedition against the power holding the straits - Rajendra Chola I against Srivijaya, to keep the China trade open. Military strategy, LO-55.
Case study on Bhaskaracharya teaching mathematics through poetic riddles in the Lilavati, and why the method worked. History of science and of teaching, goal-level CG-SST2.

Case study on a minister who left office to found a movement and built a pavilion where all genders and classes sat as equals - Basaveshvara, the anubhava mandapa, the Lingayats. LO-58 for the movement and what it rejected, LO-60 for the equality it asserted.
